resources.string: A keypair on this phone. No email, no phone number, nobody to register with — which is also why nobody can restore it for you.
Monero keys, generated here and held here. This is the money.
Small payments go straight through. Larger ones ask for your PIN. You can change where those lines sit at any time — the defaults are already cautious.
Add money when you\'re ready. Until you do, there is nothing at risk and nothing to lose.
Back it up — now, not later
One encrypted file, protected by a passphrase you choose. Keep it wherever you keep important things.
there is no way to recover it. Nobody holds a copy and there is no one to ask. That is the same reason nobody can freeze your money or take it.
It is on this phone, which is not a backup yet. Send it somewhere else: a password manager, a drive, another device.
This goes on the cards you hand out. Whoever adds you can rename you on their side, and that name is the one they see — so this is a suggestion, not an identity.
Your address goes to each contact and gets reused. Anyone reading the chain can tell the same person was paid each time — including people who only ever paid you once.
Each payment uses a fresh address, so nothing on the chain ties your payments together. Someone paying you waits for you to send a request first.
How strangers trust each other here

There is no company in the middle to take sides, so DUCAT does something simpler: both people put money up. On a ride, each of you stakes about %1$d%% of the fare. On a place to stay it is nearer %2$d%%, on a car %3$d%% — the more there is to lose, the more each side puts down.
When the deal finishes, both stakes come straight back and the fare goes to the driver. Nobody can take your stake — not the other person, not us. It only sits there, making finishing the easier choice for both of you.
Choose the file you saved and type the passphrase you set. Your identity, your money and your people come back — nothing new is created.
